How is an Iowa property tax bill worked out?

The county assessor sets an assessed value, a state percentage called the rollback turns that into taxable value, and local levy rates are applied to the taxable value. The result is the tax bill for that parcel.

Under Iowa Code 441.21, property is valued at actual value, which means fair and reasonable market value between a willing buyer and a willing seller, and is generally assessed at 100 percent of it. Sales of the property or comparable property in normal transactions must be taken into account. Abnormal sales are excluded or adjusted, and the statute names sales to immediate family, foreclosures and other forced sales, contract sales and discounted purchases as examples.

For homes, "residential" means property used mainly for habitation with two or fewer dwelling units, plus a few other housing types. Bills for a duplex or a single-family house therefore follow the same class.

What is the Iowa rollback, and why does taxable value differ from assessed value?

The rollback is a percentage the Iowa Department of Revenue certifies each year to limit growth in assessments. Taxable value is the assessed value multiplied by that percentage.

The statute never uses the word, but the idea sits in 441.21: residential and agricultural growth is tied together, so one class can rise only as fast as the other if the other grows more slowly. A county page on this topic notes that Iowa first enacted a rollback in 1977 and that the department certifies the limitation percentages to county auditors each November. The Story County rollback page links to the department's year-by-year history.

If you compare two Iowa tax statements, read both the assessed value and the taxable value lines. A seller who sees assessed value rise can still see a smaller change in taxable value.

When are Iowa property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?

Iowa property taxes are paid in two halves, and each half becomes delinquent on a set date. The first half is due before September 1 and becomes delinquent October 1. The second half is due before March 1 and becomes delinquent April 1 (445.36 and 445.37).

ItemRuleSection
First installmentDelinquent October 1, or the second business day of October if September 30 falls on a weekend445.37
Second installmentDelinquent April 1, or the second business day of April if March 31 falls on a weekend445.37
Delinquent interest1.5% per month, any part of a month counts as a full month445.39
Delinquent noticeTreasurer notifies taxpayers if an installment is unpaid on November 1445.36
Refund claim for erroneous paymentWithin two years of the due date or a final appeal decision445.60
Annual tax saleThird Monday in June446.7

A payment must reach the treasurer by the last business day of the month before the delinquency date, or be postmarked before it. Not receiving a statement does not excuse nonpayment.

What changed for Iowa homeowners under the 2026 tax law?

Senate File 2472 replaces the homestead tax credit with an exemption equal to 10% of the homestead's taxable value. The Department of Revenue says Division 20 of the 2026 Iowa Acts was signed on May 18, 2026.

  • The old credit equaled the tax on $4,850 of value. The new exemption has a $5,500 minimum and a $20,000 maximum in taxable value.
  • The maximum will be adjusted for inflation starting with assessment years on or after January 1, 2027.
  • The change applies to assessment year 2026, so the benefit shows up in taxes paid in September 2027 and March 2028.
  • The disabled veteran homestead credit remains in place for eligible veterans.

A law-firm summary of the bill also lists a roughly 2% annual growth limit on most general levies for budgets beginning July 1, 2027, a lower school foundation levy in later years, and a requirement that assessors explain residential value increases of 10% or more. See the Department of Revenue homestead page for the official summary.

How does a sale price affect an Iowa assessment?

Your sale price can become evidence of value for the parcel. When a deed is recorded, the buyer or seller submits a declaration of value to the county recorder, which enters required data and sends the forms to the assessor. The assessor keeps them three years from December 31 of the transfer year (428A.1).

Because 441.21 tells assessors to consider normal sales and to discount abnormal ones, a sale between relatives or a forced sale is treated differently from an ordinary one. Sellers who suspect the assessment is too high can use a sale record, the property's condition and nearby sales in an April protest to the board of review. Taxes on an assessment under appeal are still due on schedule, and a reduction is later credited or refunded.

Who owes the tax when an Iowa house is sold?

The tax lien attaches to the parcel, and as against a purchaser it attaches on and after June 30 each year (445.28 and 445.30). Chapter 445 has no proration rule, so the split of the current year's taxes between buyer and seller is a matter for the sale contract and closing statement.

Helpful steps before closing:

  • Ask the county treasurer for the full amount due, any tax sale and any redemption amount. A non-titleholder pays $2 per parcel per year requested (445.23).
  • Keep the statement and the receipt showing full payment, which together are conclusive evidence the parcel was clear on that date, subject to exceptions (445.24).
  • Ask whether a partial payment plan exists. Treasurers may accept partial payments held in the taxpayer's account and applied before each delinquency date (445.36A).

Partial payments cannot replace redemption after a tax sale and do not extend sale deadlines.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens at an Iowa tax sale?

At the annual sale, each delinquent parcel is offered for the total of tax, interest, fees and costs. The winning bidder is the one who will accept the smallest percentage of the parcel for that amount, with a floor of 1% (446.16).

Mailed notice goes out by regular mail no later than May 1, and failing to receive it is not a defense. If no one bids, the county bids the total due with no cash exchanged (446.19). A parcel tied to a pending municipal infraction citation or certain nuisance petitions cannot be offered (446.7).

The owner keeps the right to redeem. The certificate holder may serve notice of expiration after one year and nine months from the sale, and the right ends 90 days after service is complete (447.9 and 447.12). Redemption interest runs at 2% per month on the sale amount and later taxes (447.1). Notice must reach people with recorded interests, such as mortgagees, contract vendors and the city.

Owner-occupants who cannot pay may petition the board of supervisors, which can order the county to redeem and charge the cost back to the taxing bodies (447.9(3)).

Can a tax bill be reduced after a fire or other casualty?

Sometimes. The board of supervisors may abate or refund taxes on property destroyed by casualty, to the extent insurance does not cover it, if the parcel was not sold for taxes and was not delinquent 30 days before the loss (445.62).

The county may also compromise or abate taxes it holds on tax sale certificates by agreement or resolution (445.16). Owners of damaged houses facing a sale should ask the treasurer whether either rule applies before they set a price.

Frequently asked questions

When are Iowa property taxes due?

In two installments, with the first half due before September 1 and the second before March 1. They become delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

What is the interest rate on late Iowa property taxes?

Delinquent installments accrue interest at 1.5% per month from the delinquency date, and part of a month counts as a full month.

Does Iowa prorate property tax at closing?

Chapter 445 sets no proration rule. The buyer and seller usually settle it in the purchase contract and closing statement, and the tax lien attaches against purchasers on and after June 30.

How can I find out what is owed on an Iowa parcel?

Ask the county treasurer. The treasurer states the full tax, any tax sales and the redemption amount on request, and the treasurer mails tax statements to the titleholder.

What is the new Iowa homestead exemption?

It is an exemption equal to 10% of the homestead's taxable value, with a $5,500 minimum and a $20,000 maximum, replacing the old credit starting with assessment year 2026.

title: Iowa Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

Iowa Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Homestead Exemption: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Homestead Exemption sale
  • Turn the Iowa Homestead Exemption offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What changed with the Iowa homestead benefit in 2026?

Iowa swapped its homestead tax credit for a homestead exemption equal to 10 percent of the home's taxable value. Senate File 2472, signed May 18, 2026, made the change, according to the Iowa Department of Revenue.

The Department explains the difference this way: an exemption cuts the value you are taxed on, while a credit cuts the tax bill directly. The old credit equaled the levy on the first $4,850 of a home's value, with a floor of $62.50, under Iowa Code 425.1.

The change reaches back to assessment year 2026. It shows up on the property taxes paid in September 2027 and March 2028.

How much is the Iowa homestead exemption worth?

The exemption is 10 percent of taxable value, with a minimum of $5,500 and a maximum of $20,000 of taxable value. Starting with assessment years that begin on or after January 1, 2027, the $20,000 maximum is adjusted for inflation.

FeatureDetail
Rate10 percent of taxable value
Minimum exemption$5,500 of taxable value
Maximum exemption$20,000 of taxable value in 2026, indexed from 2027
Extra for age 65 and older$6,500 of taxable value
First applies toAssessment year 2026

Here is how the floor and cap play out. A house with a taxable value of $40,000 would get $5,500 instead of $4,000. A house with a taxable value of $250,000 would get $20,000 instead of $25,000. Those figures are illustrations of the rule, not quotes from any county.

The benefit is a reduction in taxable value, so the dollars saved depend on your local levy.

Who qualifies for the Iowa homestead exemption?

The owner must live in Iowa and occupy the home. County assessors describe the test as living there on July 1 and for at least six months of every year. The extra exemption for older owners requires the owner to be 65 or older on January 1 of the year of the application, per the Des Moines County assessor.

Other points that affect eligibility:

  • Owners who were already getting the credit before July 1, 2026 are awarded the 10 percent exemption automatically if they still qualify.
  • Owners 65 or older who qualify for the additional exemption do not have to refile each year.
  • The disabled veteran homestead credit remains in place and was not eliminated by the new law.

Iowa also has a military exemption for qualifying veterans, Guard members and reservists, and a family farm credit for tracts of 10 acres or more that are farmed by the owner or immediate family. Each has its own filing rules at the assessor's office.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How and when do I file for the homestead exemption?

Applications are due on or before July 1 of the year the exemption is first claimed. The form is Homestead Tax Exemption 54-028, linked from the Department of Revenue page, and it goes to your county assessor.

You only need to file once. The Des Moines County assessor says the exemption continues until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies. The family farm credit has a different date, November 1.

If you bought the house this spring, ask the assessor about the July 1 date before it passes.

How much land counts toward an Iowa homestead?

The home itself plus up to one-half acre inside a city plat or up to forty acres outside one. The Department of Revenue set this out in a June 2026 notice to assessors and auditors.

When a parcel has more land than the limit, the land value is scaled down before the exemption is figured. The notice gives an example of a two-acre parcel inside a city plat: its $10,000 land value is cut to $2,500 for homestead purposes.

The disabled veteran credit is narrower. For applications submitted on or after July 1, 2026, it covers the dwelling without appurtenances plus one-half acre, whether or not the land is in a plat.

Sellers of rural Iowa houses should look at this closely. A house on an 80-acre parcel is not fully covered, so the tax bill on the whole parcel can look different from a town lot.

What happens to the homestead exemption when you sell the house?

It ends with the sale. The assessor's rule is that the exemption lasts until the property is sold or the owner stops qualifying, and the buyer files for their own.

That has a few practical effects at closing:

  • Property tax for the sale year is still billed in two installments, delinquent after September 30 and March 31 under Iowa Code 445.37.
  • The seller's share of the current installment is normally settled between buyer and seller through the closing statement.
  • Moving out before July 1 can affect whether you meet the occupancy test for that year.

If you are selling because you cannot keep up with taxes or repairs, a cash sale can shorten the time you carry the house. Our Iowa property tax guide covers appeals and what happens when taxes go unpaid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What other 2026 Iowa property tax changes affect home sellers?

Several rules changed alongside the exemption. The Iowa League of Cities summary of SF 2472 lists the following.

  • The residential rollback for fiscal year 2027 is 44.5345 percent.
  • Homes with three or more dwelling units move into a restored multi-residential class on January 1, 2027. Duplexes and single-family homes stay residential.
  • Property is generally assessed every two years.
  • Starting January 1, 2027, the burden of proof shifts to the assessor when an assessment increases by more than 10 percent.
  • State funding for the old credit phases out between July 1, 2027 and July 1, 2029.

A property tax protest is filed with the local board of review from April 2 through April 30, under Iowa Code 441.37. In a county under a disaster declaration, the window moves to May 1 through June 5.

Which new Iowa laws change how a house sale works?

Two Iowa laws that took effect July 1, 2026 touch ordinary home sales. Iowa Realtors summarized them in its overview of new laws.

  • Under SF 2448, homeowners associations must certify whether dues are current and disclose approved upcoming assessments and transfer-related fees.
  • After a buyer asks for repairs based on an inspection, the seller can request the matching sections of the report. If they are not supplied, the seller may cancel the contract without penalty.
  • Under SF 2472, a new FirstHome Iowa savings account lets first-time buyers set money aside for down payments and closing costs.

These rules mostly matter to sellers who list with an agent and negotiate repairs. A direct as-is sale skips the repair-request step.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Iowa homestead exemption?

It is 10 percent of your home's taxable value, no less than $5,500 and no more than $20,000 for assessment year 2026. The cap is adjusted for inflation starting with assessment years that begin in 2027.

Do I need to reapply if I already get the Iowa homestead credit?

No. Owners who received the homestead credit or exemption before July 1, 2026 are automatically awarded the 10 percent exemption if they are still eligible.

What is the deadline to claim the Iowa homestead exemption?

July 1 of the year you first claim it. You file Form 54-028 with your county assessor.

Does the homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. It continues only until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies, so the new owner must apply on their own.

How much extra do homeowners age 65 and older get?

An additional $6,500 of taxable value. You must be 65 or older by January 1 of the assessment year, and you do not refile in later years.

Is the disabled veteran credit gone?

No. The Department of Revenue says the disabled veteran homestead tax credit is not eliminated by SF 2472. For applications on or after July 1, 2026, it covers the dwelling plus one-half acre.

title: Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax sale
  • Turn the Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Iowa have an estate tax or an inheritance tax today?

Iowa has neither one for a person who dies now. The state estate tax stopped applying to deaths on or after January 1, 2005, and the inheritance tax stopped applying to deaths on or after January 1, 2025, according to the Iowa Department of Revenue.

The two taxes work differently, and heirs often mix them up. An estate tax is charged on the whole estate. Iowa's inheritance tax was based on what each beneficiary had a right to receive, which is why the rate depended on who the heir was.

For anyone who inherits an Iowa house now, the practical result is simple: no Iowa death tax return stands between the heirs and a sale. Other costs still apply, and the sections below cover them.

How was the Iowa inheritance tax phased out?

The Legislature cut the tax in steps over four years and then ended it. Under Iowa Code 450.10(7), the normal rates were reduced by a set percentage depending on the year of death.

Year of deathRate reduction
202120 percent
202240 percent
202360 percent
202480 percent
2025 and laterChapter does not apply

The end point is written into chapter 450, which says it does not apply to property of estates of decedents dying on or after January 1, 2025. The tax on unknown heirs was cut on the same schedule and ended for 2025 deaths too.

If the person who owned the house died in 2024 or earlier, the old rules can still matter, so keep reading.

Who paid inheritance tax before 2025, and who was exempt?

Close family paid nothing. Property passing to a surviving spouse, parents and grandparents, children, stepchildren, grandchildren and other lineal descendants was exempt under chapter 450.

Everyone else could owe tax, and the rate climbed with the amount received. The statute set these brackets before the phase-down reductions:

  • Siblings, sons-in-law and daughters-in-law: 5 percent on the first $12,500, rising by bracket to 10 percent on amounts above $150,000.
  • Other heirs, such as nieces, nephews, cousins and friends: 10 percent up to $50,000, 12 percent to $100,000 and 15 percent above that.
  • Out-of-state charitable bodies: 10 percent on the full amount.
  • For-profit firms and corporations: 15 percent on the full amount.

Some transfers were left out altogether. An estate of $25,000 or less after debts owed no tax, tangible personal property was exempt when the total was $5,000 or less, and gifts to qualifying charitable, educational and religious groups were excluded.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What deadlines applied to an Iowa inheritance tax return?

The tax came due on the last day of the ninth month after the date of death, and the return was due the same day unless none was required. The Department's own page says the beneficiary was responsible for the tax on earlier deaths.

The Department of Revenue could extend payment for up to ten years from the end of the month of death to avoid hardship, but interest ran from the original date. Late payment also carried a penalty.

These dates only matter now for an older death. A house inherited from someone who died in, say, 2023 can still carry an open file, which is worth checking before closing.

Can an old inheritance tax lien still affect selling an inherited Iowa house?

It can, for deaths before 2025. Under Iowa Code 450.7, the tax was a lien on the taxable estate and the decedent's property from the date of death until paid, and a sale did not wipe it out.

The same section says the lien generally ends ten years after death, and it ranks ahead of later mortgages, buyers and judgment creditors without any recorded notice. Property passing to a spouse, parents, children and other lineal descendants was never subject to the lien.

Ways the lien was released or cleared:

  • Filing a receipt showing the tax was paid with the clerk of court.
  • Filing a certificate that no tax was owed.
  • Filing a release or waiver.
  • Where no return was required, filing an affidavit describing the real estate in the county where it sits (section 450.22).

A title company or estate attorney normally handles this paperwork. If you are an heir selling a house from a pre-2025 death, ask them whether anything is still open of record.

Does the federal estate tax reach an Iowa house?

Only for very large estates. The IRS lists a filing threshold of $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026 and $13,990,000 for 2025, as shown on its estate tax page.

An estate must file a federal return when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, goes above that figure. A surviving spouse can also elect to carry over the unused exemption of the person who died. That election is made on a timely filed estate tax return.

Most Iowa families who inherit a house will fall far below the threshold. The house is one asset among others in that total, and a sale price does not by itself trigger a filing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What property taxes still follow an inherited Iowa home?

Ordinary property tax continues whether or not anyone owes a death tax. Iowa counties bill in two installments, and the first becomes delinquent on October 1 and the second on April 1, under Iowa Code 445.37. If the last day of September or March falls on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the next month.

Heirs sometimes assume the homestead benefit passes along with the house. It does not run on its own. The Des Moines County assessor explains that once a person qualifies, the exemption continues until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies, so an heir who will not live there may be taxed without it. Our Iowa homestead exemption guide covers the 2026 change.

Plan for the taxes due on the estate's calendar. A cash buyer can usually close ahead of an installment date, and the settlement figures show what is paid from proceeds.

What does selling an inherited house in Iowa involve now?

The steps depend on how title is held and on whether a court-supervised estate is open. If the owner died with a will or without one, the person with authority over the estate signs the deed, and the buyer's title company will ask for proof of that authority.

Recording the deed also triggers the Iowa transfer tax, set by Iowa Code 428A.1 at eighty cents for each $500 of value above the first $500. It is paid to the county recorder, and a declaration of value goes in with the deed. Transfers with no consideration are not taxed.

  • Gather the death certificate and any will.
  • Confirm who has authority to sell, whether an executor or heirs holding title.
  • Ask the title company to search for liens, including any pre-2025 inheritance tax lien.
  • Check which property tax installment is next.

We buy inherited Iowa houses as they stand, which helps when the home needs repairs the heirs would rather not fund.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an inheritance tax in Iowa in 2026?

No. Iowa's Department of Revenue states that the inheritance tax does not apply to deaths occurring on or after January 1, 2025, so a 2026 death creates no Iowa inheritance tax return.

Does Iowa have a state estate tax?

No. The Iowa estate tax does not apply to deaths on or after January 1, 2005. The federal estate tax is separate and has a 2026 filing threshold of $15,000,000.

Do I owe Iowa inheritance tax if my parent died in 2024?

A child inheriting from a parent owed nothing, because property passing to children and other lineal descendants was exempt under chapter 450. Siblings and other heirs could owe a tax at rates reduced by 80 percent for 2024 deaths.

Can an inheritance tax lien block a sale of the house?

It can for older deaths. The lien under section 450.7 generally ends ten years after death, but it can be released earlier by a receipt, certificate or waiver, and a title company can tell you whether one is on record.

Who pays the Iowa transfer tax when an inherited house is sold?

Settle that point in the purchase contract with your title company.

Do heirs keep the homestead exemption on an inherited Iowa house?

Not automatically. County assessors say the exemption continues only while the owner still qualifies, and it ends when the property is sold.

title: Iowa Sheriff Sales: Foreclosure Sale Steps and Redemption
content:
Iowa Sheriff Sales: Foreclosure Sale Steps and Redemption

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What is an Iowa sheriff sale and who runs it?

An Iowa sheriff sale is the public auction of a property after a court has ordered it sold to pay a debt, and the county sheriff conducts it. For a home loan, the road to that auction runs through the district court, because Iowa mortgages can be foreclosed only by a court action in equity, with one narrow exception for a voluntary agreement (Iowa Code chapter 654).

The court enters judgment for the full amount due and orders the property sold as needed to satisfy it. The sale is then made under a special execution. Whether the former owner gets a redemption period afterward depends on which kind of foreclosure the lender chose, which is covered below.

Judgments from other creditors can also end in a sheriff sale, because Iowa enforces money judgments by execution against real estate. Chapter 626 sets the notice and auction rules for both situations, so the steps below apply whichever debt started the case.

What has to happen before the sheriff can sell an Iowa home?

Before a lender files, Iowa requires specific notices, and they differ depending on the property. A skipped notice is often the first thing an owner or attorney checks.

  • One- and two-family residences: a written notice of the right to cure, with thirty days from the notice to bring the loan current, and no acceleration until that time passes (section 654.2D). There is no cure right if a proper notice was given for a default within the previous 365 days.
  • Farmland: a notice of right to cure and a 45-day wait before enforcement (section 654.2A). For farm debt of $20,000 or more, a mediation release is generally needed first (sections 654.2C and 654A.11).
  • Owner-occupied homes: the lender must tell the owner about counseling and mediation on a form the attorney general prescribes, and must give a fourteen-day demand for payment of the accelerated balance to qualify for attorney fees (section 654.4B).

If the court finds the counseling notice was never served and the owner asks for counseling or mediation, the sale can be delayed. That delay cannot exceed sixty days under section 654.4B.

How much notice does an Iowa sheriff sale get?

Real estate sold by a sheriff needs four weeks of notice, posted and published. The table gathers the main timing rules in one place.

RuleWhat the statute saysSection
Notice periodFour weeks before the sale626.74
PostingAt least three public places in the county, one of them the courthouse626.75
NewspaperFirst publication at least four weeks before the sale626.75
Occupying debtorWritten notice served at least twenty days before the sale626.78
Hours of the auctionBetween 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.626.80
Junior creditor requestProof of service filed at least ten days before the sale654.15A

A sheriff who sells without the required notice forfeits $100 to the defendant plus actual damages, but the sale itself stays valid (section 626.77). A sale made without the twenty-day notice to an occupying debtor can be set aside on motion within ninety days (section 626.79). The statutes are on the Iowa Legislature site.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How does the auction itself work?

The sheriff sells at public auction between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., and the start time and place must appear in the notice. The statute names no single location, so the notice is the only reliable place to find it.

Sealed written bids are allowed. The sheriff receipts them, keeps them sealed until the auction begins, then opens and announces them. If a winning written bidder does not pay in certified funds as the notice directs, the bid is canceled and the sheriff certifies the next highest bidder, within 24 hours for an electronic transfer or 48 hours otherwise (section 626.80).

The sale can be postponed. The sheriff may do so when there are no bidders, when the offer is grossly inadequate, when the judgment creditor asks, or when the parties agree. Without a written agreement, no more than two adjournments of up to sixty days each are allowed (section 626.81).

Two more details matter to owners. A debtor can deliver a signed plan of division before 9:00 a.m. on the sale day so that only the land needed to cover the debt is sold (section 626.84). And any money left after the debt and costs goes to the debtor, unless another execution or valid lien claims it (section 626.82).

How long can an owner redeem after an Iowa sheriff sale?

The default is one year from the day of sale, and the owner keeps possession during that time. The first six months belong to the debtor alone (section 628.3). If the debtor does not redeem, a mortgagee or qualifying creditor may redeem within nine months of the sale (section 628.5).

Shorter periods apply in several situations, so the table is worth checking against the court papers.

SituationRedemption periodSection
Standard saleOne year; debtor alone for six months628.3
Mortgage under 10 acres, if the mortgage provides and the lender waives a deficiencySix months, or three months if not agricultural628.26
Under 10 acres, abandoned, mortgage provides, deficiency waivedSixty days628.27
Non-agricultural, non-residential property180 days; 90 days with a deficiency waiver628.28
Former one- or two-family residence the debtor no longer occupies30 days, or 60 with junior creditors628.28
Foreclosure without redemption elected by the plaintiffNone after the sale654.23

Redeeming a sold home frees it from liability for any unpaid judgment balance (section 628.3). Because the periods differ so much, the dates in the decree and the sheriff's certificate control, not a general rule of thumb.

What is foreclosure without redemption in Iowa?

It is an election the plaintiff can make, on property not used for agriculture, to skip the post-sale redemption period (sections 654.20 through 654.23). The petition has to carry a required notice on its first page.

The owner can answer by filing a demand to delay the sale before judgment. The sale then comes two months after judgment, or six months for a one- or two-family residence, or three months if the petition waives a deficiency judgment (section 654.21). With no demand, the sale is held promptly after judgment.

Once the sale happens, the mortgagor has no right to redeem, and junior lienholders lose theirs too. When someone other than the mortgagee buys, junior liens are extinguished (section 654.23). For a one- or two-family residence with no deficiency waiver and no demand for delay, the plaintiff cannot seek a deficiency judgment (section 654.26).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens to the people living in the house?

The owner stays in the home through the redemption period, but once it ends and a deed issues, the former owner can be removed by a court order. A defendant who stays in possession after a foreclosure or execution sale is subject to forcible entry and detainer, unless that person claims paramount title (section 648.1).

  • Written notice to quit: three days before suing (section 648.3).
  • Hearing: set no later than 8 days from filing, or 15 if the plaintiff asks or agrees to a later date (section 648.5).
  • Removal: the execution issues within 3 days of judgment and can be carried out only in the daytime (sections 648.20 and 648.22).

The removal steps run on short clocks, so an owner who wants to choose how the house changes hands has the most room before the sale date.

Can I sell an Iowa house before the sheriff sale?

An owner can generally sell to a buyer at any point before the auction, as long as the sale pays off what the judgment and liens require. A sale closing before the auction can end the case without a sheriff's deed.

Iowa law offers a few related paths. During a pending foreclosure, the plaintiff may ask the court to approve a commercially reasonable sale free of liens, with net proceeds held in escrow (section 654.17A). Before a sheriff's deed is recorded, the judgment creditor may rescind the foreclosure by filing a notice and a $50 fee (section 654.17). A voluntary nonjudicial foreclosure under section 654.18 needs a written agreement from both sides, and the mortgagor gets a five-business-day right to cancel.

The seller of a house in Iowa is liable for the state transfer tax, which is 80 cents for each $500 of value above the first $500 (sections 428A.1 and 428A.3). Cash Home Buyers can look at an Iowa house as-is while the foreclosure is still pending, and you decide whether the numbers work. Talk with an Iowa attorney about your own case first, because the dates in your decree are what count.

Frequently asked questions

Who runs an Iowa sheriff sale?

The sheriff of the county where the property sits runs it. The sale follows a court judgment, and the notice sets the date, start time and place.

How many weeks of notice does Iowa require for a sheriff sale?

Four weeks. The notice must be posted in at least three public places in the county, including the courthouse, and published in a newspaper with the first run at least four weeks before the sale.

Can the owner stay in the house after the sheriff sale?

Usually yes, during the redemption period. The debtor keeps possession while redemption is open, though the period can be as short as 30 days in some cases and nonexistent when foreclosure without redemption was elected.

Is there a deficiency judgment after an Iowa foreclosure?

Sometimes. If the sale does not cover the judgment, a general execution may issue against the mortgagor unless the parties agreed otherwise, but a one- or two-family residence with no deficiency waiver and no demand for delay is protected from a deficiency (sections 654.6 and 654.26).

Can a sheriff sale be postponed?

Yes. The sheriff can postpone for no bidders, a grossly inadequate offer, or a request from the judgment creditor. Without written agreement, two adjournments of up to sixty days each is the limit.

title: Iowa Quitclaim Deed: Recording, Fees and When It Works
content:
Iowa Quitclaim Deed: Recording, Fees and When It Works

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Quitclaim Deed: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Quitclaim Deed sale
  • Turn the Iowa Quitclaim Deed offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What does an Iowa quitclaim deed actually transfer?

It transfers whatever interest the person signing holds, and nothing more is promised. Under Iowa Code 558.19, the sample quitclaim form states a consideration in dollars and says the grantor quitclaims to the grantee all interest in a described tract.

The statute offers other sample forms for comparison. The fee simple deed without warranty uses the words "hereby convey," and the warranty deed adds a warranty of title against all persons. Each form is called sufficient if varied to suit the circumstances, so the quitclaim is a legally valid choice. The difference is the promise the grantor makes.

That is why a quitclaim fits transfers between people who already know the property's history, such as adding a spouse or moving a house into a family arrangement. It fits less well when a stranger is paying money and expects a promise about title.

What does it cost to record a quitclaim deed in an Iowa county?

Recording usually costs $5 per page plus two $1 charges, and transfer tax may add to that if money changed hands. The recorder's schedule comes from Iowa Code 331.604.

ChargeAmount
Recording, real estate instrument$5 per page or fraction, per transaction
Records management fund$1 per recorded transaction
Electronic transaction fund$1 per recorded transaction
Transfer tax80 cents per $500 or fraction over the first $500 of consideration
Groundwater hazard statementNo recorder fee

Counties may add services or rules of their own, so call the recorder before you mail a deed.

How should an Iowa quitclaim deed be formatted for the recorder?

Each recorder sets format requirements, and one county's published list is a good guide. The Story County Recorder asks for the following on deeds:

  • A minimum of three inches of blank space at the top of the first page.
  • The preparer's name, address and phone number typed directly below that space.
  • The line "Address Tax Statement To" with the taxpayer's name and address, directly under the preparer information.
  • A full legal description. The shortened description on a tax statement should not be used.
  • Printed names beneath every signature, including the acknowledging officer.
  • A signed, dated and notarized document that is legible and reproducible.

Other counties may differ in small ways. You can see the Story County recording requirements for the full list.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who must notarize an Iowa deed, and can it be done remotely?

A deed must be acknowledged before a notarial officer before it can be lawfully recorded (558.42), and the acknowledgment must follow Chapter 9B (558.20). The signer declares before the officer that the signature is theirs and given for the stated purpose, and an entity signer must have authority.

Under Chapter 9B, the officer must confirm identity through personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence. Accepted evidence includes a passport, driver's license or government nondriver ID that is current or expired no more than three years, or a credible witness. The officer may refuse if not satisfied that the signer has capacity or signs knowingly and voluntarily.

Remote notarization is allowed under 9B.14A. The notary and signer must communicate by sight and sound, identity needs personal knowledge, a credible witness or two types of identity proofing, and the notary must make and keep an audio-visual recording for at least ten years. The certificate must state that technology was used. Check with the recorder that the county accepts the resulting document.

When does a quitclaim deed owe Iowa transfer tax?

Transfer tax applies only when there is consideration above $500. The tax is 80 cents for each $500 or fraction over $500, and the person who conveys the property is liable (428A.1 and 428A.3).

Many family and court-driven transfers are exempt under 428A.2. The ones most relevant to quitclaims include:

  • Deeds between spouses, or between parent and child, without actual consideration. Cancelling debt secured by the property is not actual consideration if it does not exceed the property's fair market value.
  • Deeds between former spouses under a dissolution decree.
  • Deeds that correct, confirm or supplement a recorded deed without added consideration.
  • Deeds returning property to lienholders in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Deeds distributing trust assets to beneficiaries without consideration.

A recorder will not record an exempt deed without a signed statement claiming the exemption, filed with the deed or endorsed on it (428A.4). Knowingly failing to pay due tax, or willfully entering false information on a declaration of value, is a simple misdemeanor (428A.10 and 428A.15).

What is the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement?

Both are forms that go in with a deed. The declaration of value states the full consideration, must be signed by at least one seller or buyer or an agent, and is required unless the instrument falls in an exempt category. The recorder does not record it. The data goes to the assessor (428A.1).

The groundwater hazard statement under 558.69 covers known burial sites, wells, solid waste disposal sites, underground storage tanks, hazardous waste and private sewage systems. The owner is responsible for accuracy. If no such conditions exist, the first page of the deed must carry the exemption statement. A recorder must refuse the deed if the required statement is missing, although a recording made without it does not void the deed.

Story County's page notes that the groundwater process changed on July 1, 2022 under House File 2343, so use the current form from the recorder.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Does a spouse have to sign an Iowa quitclaim deed?

Often yes. If the owner is married, a conveyance of the homestead is not valid unless the other spouse signs the same or a like instrument, or a power of attorney for it (561.13).

A spouse who holds only homestead rights and a statutory share may relinquish those rights specifically under 597.5 without joining the granting clause. The requirement does not apply if a dissolution decree ended the interest, if the right of recovery is barred under 614.15, for a purchase-money mortgage, or where a court of equity finds that invalidating the transaction would unjustly enrich the other spouse.

The homestead is the owner's home and the contiguous land used with it. Inside a city plat it is limited to one half acre, and outside a plat to forty acres (561.1 and 561.2).

When should a quitclaim deed not be the tool for selling an Iowa house?

An unrecorded instrument is invalid against later good-faith purchasers for value without notice, so recording the deed promptly protects the new owner (558.41). Transfers by quitclaim deed are also excluded from the seller disclosure requirement, which is one reason families use them between relatives.

Other recording rules can apply by property type. Entity transfers carry implied warranties unless the instrument says otherwise, including that the entity exists and the signer is authorized (558.72). Agricultural land conveyances must be recorded by the grantee within 180 days (558.44).

If the plan is to sell, ask the buyer or title company which form they want before you sign anything. Owners with liens, back taxes or unclear co-owners often need advice before deciding.

Frequently asked questions

Is a quitclaim deed legal in Iowa?

Yes. Iowa Code 558.19 lists the quitclaim form with fee simple deeds without warranty and with warranty as sufficient forms of conveyance.

What does it cost to record an Iowa quitclaim deed?

Recording is $5 per page or fraction, plus $1 for the records management fund and $1 for the electronic transaction fund per recorded transaction. Transfer tax applies only if consideration exceeds $500.

Does a quitclaim deed need to be notarized in Iowa?

Yes. A deed must be acknowledged under Chapter 9B before it can be lawfully recorded, and remote notarization is allowed if the statutory conditions are met.

Does a quitclaim deed remove my spouse's homestead rights?

Not by itself. A married owner's homestead conveyance is invalid without the spouse's signature on the same or a like instrument, with limited exceptions.

Can I quitclaim my house to my child without paying transfer tax in Iowa?

A deed between parent and child without actual consideration is exempt under 428A.2, but the exemption must be claimed in a signed statement and you may still owe recording fees.

title: Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House
content:
Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House sale
  • Turn the Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Iowa have a separate capital gains tax on a house sale?

No. Iowa does not charge a stand-alone capital gains tax. The profit from selling a house is reported as part of your Iowa individual income tax return, and for tax year 2026 the Department of Revenue says one flat rate of 3.8 percent applies to all levels of taxable income.

On the Iowa return, the capital gain or loss line starts with 100 percent of the amount from your federal Form 1040. The state says the capital gain deduction is not taken on that line, because a qualifying deduction goes on a separate line. If your federal return needs Schedule D and Form 8949, a copy goes with the Iowa return.

One note to avoid confusion: the 3.8 percent Iowa rate and the 3.8 percent federal net investment income tax share a number and nothing else. They are separate taxes with separate rules, and both can matter on a large gain.

How much gain on your Iowa home can you exclude?

If the house was your main home, you can generally exclude up to $250,000 of gain, or up to $500,000 on a joint return. Iowa says it generally follows the federal rules on excluding gain from a principal residence, so the federal exclusion also keeps that gain off your Iowa taxable income.

The IRS sets two tests, and you must meet both:

  • Ownership: you or your spouse owned the home for at least 24 months of the five years before the sale.
  • Use: you, and your spouse if filing jointly, each lived in it as a main home for at least 24 months of that same five-year period.

The two 24-month periods do not need to be the same months. Generally you cannot use the exclusion if you excluded gain from another home sale during the two years before this one. The IRS points to Publication 523 for exceptions and partial exclusions.

You must report the sale if you receive a Form 1099-S, even if the full gain is excludable, and if you cannot exclude all of the gain. Use Form 8949 with Schedule D.

What happens if the gain is larger than the exclusion?

Gain above the exclusion is taxed federally as a capital gain and in Iowa at the flat state rate. The federal rate depends on how long you held the property.

ItemRule from the source
Held one year or lessShort-term, taxed as ordinary income
Held more than one yearLong-term, federal rates of 0, 15 or 20 percent by taxable income
Unrecaptured section 1250 gain (depreciation on real property)Maximum federal rate of 25 percent
Iowa individual income tax, 20263.8 percent flat
Iowa interest on overdue tax, from January 1, 202610 percent a year, 0.8 percent a month

The federal net investment income tax is 3.8 percent for single filers above $200,000, joint filers above $250,000 and separate filers above $125,000 of modified adjusted gross income. The IRS says the tax does not apply to the part of a home sale gain that is excluded as a principal residence. Gain above the exclusion can be hit.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Which Iowa capital gain deductions were repealed?

Most Iowa capital gain deductions ended with tax year 2023. The Department of Revenue states that the repealed categories include gains from selling real estate used in a non-farm business, an entire business, timber, cattle, horses or breeding livestock (with an exception for retired farmers), and employer securities sold to a qualified Iowa employee stock ownership plan.

The change took effect January 1, 2023. Installment sales that began before that date still qualify for the deduction. The Department's deduction page still carries reference material for non-farm real property, but the state's 2023 changes page controls, and the statute governs in any dispute.

That matters to anyone who read older guidance that gave a ten-year holding rule for business real estate. If you sold rental or commercial property after 2022, do not rely on it.

  • Retired farmers aged 55 or older may still deduct gain from farm real estate if they materially participated in farming for ten years in total.
  • A retired farmer has a single lifetime election.
  • Electing the deduction blocks the beginning farmer tax credit and the farm lease income exclusion.
  • Gain from an employee-owned corporation's stock has its own phase-in: 33 percent excluded for 2023, 66 percent for 2024 and 100 percent from 2025.

A house in town or a rental house is not covered by those farm rules. A principal residence relies on the federal exclusion instead.

How does an inherited Iowa house change the gain?

Inherited property generally takes a new tax basis equal to its fair market value on the date of the owner's death, not the price the deceased originally paid. A sale soon after inheritance often produces little or no taxable gain for that reason.

The estate's personal representative can instead elect an alternate valuation date, which uses the value on that date. If you did not receive a Schedule A (Form 8971), the IRS says you can use the appraised value at death for state inheritance or transmission tax purposes. Property given to the decedent within one year before death can carry the decedent's adjusted basis rather than the death-date value.

Keep an appraisal from the date of death. It is the first document a tax preparer will ask for if you sell a house you inherited in Iowa, and it is hard to recreate later.

Do nonresidents owe Iowa tax on a house they sell in Iowa?

Yes, if the Iowa-source income reaches the filing trigger. The Department of Revenue lists capital gain on the sale of Iowa property, along with rental income, as income from Iowa property. A nonresident or part-year resident must file when Iowa-source net income is $1,000 or more, unless income falls under the standard thresholds.

For the 2025 return year those thresholds were more than $9,000 for single or married filing separately filers, and more than $13,500 for joint filers, head of household and qualifying surviving spouse. Higher amounts apply to people 65 and older.

People who sell an Iowa house after moving away, or heirs living out of state, often miss this step. Check it before the money is spent.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Iowa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What other Iowa costs show up when a house is sold?

Iowa property tax and state transfer tax are separate from any income tax on the gain. Real estate transfer tax applies to a deed that conveys Iowa real estate when the consideration exceeds $500, at 80 cents for each $500 or fractional part above $500, under Iowa Code 428A.1. The code treats the full price as consideration, including any lien the buyer assumes.

  • A declaration of value, signed by at least one buyer or seller, goes to the county recorder with the deed.
  • Personal property is presumed part of the price unless its value is stated on the instrument.
  • Property tax on Iowa homes runs a year behind and is billed in September and March.
  • A seller closing from July 1 to December 31 owes the September installment, and one closing from January 1 to June 30 owes the March one.

An as-is cash sale does not change these rules. It changes who pays for repairs and how fast the deal closes.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a capital gains tax in Iowa?

Iowa has no separate capital gains tax. Gains are part of Iowa taxable income, which is taxed at a flat 3.8 percent for tax year 2026.

Do I pay Iowa tax on the sale of my primary residence?

Only on gain above the exclusion. Iowa generally follows the federal rule that lets you exclude up to $250,000, or $500,000 on a joint return, if you meet the ownership and use tests.

Can I deduct capital gains on a rental house sold in Iowa?

Not under the old non-farm real property deduction. The Department of Revenue says that deduction was repealed for tax years starting January 1, 2023, apart from installment sales begun before then.

Does Iowa tax gain when I inherit and sell a house?

Gain is measured from the stepped-up basis, usually the fair market value at the date of death. If you sell at about that value, little gain results.

Iowa Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property sale

Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Does every Iowa house go through probate when the owner dies?

No. The Iowa Judicial Branch states that opening an estate is not required for every deceased person. An estate may be needed to transfer property, pay debts or obtain tax clearances, and a house titled only in the decedent's name usually needs some court step before it can be sold or retitled.

Probate in Iowa runs through the district court in the county, and the clerk of court is the first office to call. The courts' own FAQ says a valid will must be in writing, signed by the maker and witnessed by two people. If you cannot find a will, it suggests checking with the clerk in the county where it may be stored, any attorney who drafted it, safe deposit boxes, and the named executor. The Iowa Judicial Branch probate FAQ has the details.

Who can open an Iowa estate, and how soon?

A surviving spouse, an heir, a creditor or another person with good grounds may petition for appointment. Iowa Code 633.227 and 633.228 give priority by class: the surviving spouse has 20 days from the death to file, and each other class has 10 days, with a class's window moving up if nobody exists in the class before it.

Whoever serves must meet the basic test in 633.63: a natural person of full age, not incompetent and not found unsuitable by the court. Under 633.3, "full age" means 18, or having married. A court can remove a fiduciary on a verified petition under 633.65.

For a family with several heirs, the practical point is simple. Agree early on who will be the personal representative, because that person signs the sale papers and answers to the court.

What deadlines and costs show up in an Iowa estate?

The statute sets several clocks that matter to a family planning to sell a house.

ItemFigureSection
Hearing noticeAt least 20 days after service, unless good cause shortens it633.40
Inventory and report90 days after the personal representative qualifies, unless extended633.361
Creditor claimsLater of four months after the second published notice or one month after mailed notice633.410
Spouse's electionFour months after service of notice633.237
Court cost0.2% of probate assets listed in the inventory633.31
Outside limit for openingClaims are barred if administration has not started within five years of death633.413
Delinquent filingsClerk notices go out June 1 and December 1; 60 days to file633.32

The 0.2% court cost leaves out joint tenancy property, lifetime transfers, life insurance payable to a beneficiary and real estate outside Iowa.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Iowa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who inherits an Iowa house when there is no will?

Iowa intestacy law sends the house first to a surviving spouse, then down a list of relatives. The split depends on whether the children are also the spouse's children.

  • No children, or all children shared with the spouse: the spouse takes the real property the decedent held during the marriage, subject to exceptions such as judicial sales (633.211).
  • Some children are not the spouse's: the spouse takes one half of the real property, and the estate tops up the spouse's total to $50,000 if the share falls short (633.212).
  • No spouse: the order runs to children, then parents, then siblings' descendants, then grandparents, then great-grandparents, and finally escheat to the state (633.219).

In an intestate estate the spouse may elect a life estate in the homestead instead (633.240). A homestead inside a city plat is limited to one half acre, and outside a plat to forty acres (561.2).

When can the personal representative sell the house?

The personal representative can sell estate real estate to pay debts, distribute the estate or serve the estate's best interests, but exempt personal property and the homestead are carved out and follow their own rules (633.386). If the homestead is not set off to the spouse and the spouse has not chosen to occupy it, it can be sold under the court-directed provisions.

Several features of a sale are worth knowing before you speak with a buyer:

  • Notice of a sale petition goes to interested persons unless they waive it in writing or all of them are personal representatives who signed the petition (633.389).
  • A sale on credit for more than twelve months needs a hearing on notice (633.392).
  • A public auction is advertised once a week for two consecutive weeks in a county newspaper, with the last notice one to seven days before the sale (633.397).
  • Sale proceeds are held by the personal representative, subject to any rights of the spouse or children, unless those rights are waived (633.386).

A title company or buyer may ask the representative to prove authority. Under 633.78, a third party has 10 business days to verify a fiduciary's authority, and an unjustified refusal can lead to penalties from $500 to $10,000 plus damages.

Why the small estate affidavit usually does not help with a house

Iowa's affidavit procedure for very small estates applies only if the decedent's personal property totals $50,000 or less and there is no real property. Because a house is real property, this shortcut rarely works for a family that wants to sell one.

The procedure also needs at least forty days to have passed since the death, a sworn affidavit and a certified death certificate, and it cannot be used while an administration is pending (633.356). For deaths before January 1, 2025, real property passing to people exempt from inheritance tax as joint tenants with survivorship rights also qualified.

If the house was held in joint tenancy with a surviving owner, no probate may be needed to move title. Ask the county recorder or an attorney what filing proves the survivor's ownership.

How do creditor claims affect a house sale in an Iowa estate?

Creditors have a limited window to file, and that window shapes when an estate can safely close. Notice is published once a week for two weeks in a local newspaper, and known claimants whose claims may not be paid in administration receive mailed notice (633.230).

Claims not filed by the later of four months after the second publication or one month after mailing are barred, with statutory exceptions (633.410). The representative may still pay valid debts that were never filed, at the representative's own risk (633.435). Property other than the homestead and exempt property is chargeable with the debts and costs of the estate (633.350).

That chargeability is why heirs who want a fast sale should talk to the estate's attorney before distributing money. A house sold early can pay the debts, and the remainder can be shared.

Does Iowa still have an inheritance tax on a house?

No tax applies to estates of people who died on or after January 1, 2025. Section 450.98 says the chapter does not apply to the property of those decedents.

The old rules still matter for deaths before 2025. Spouses, lineal ascendants and descendants and stepchildren were exempt. Brothers, sisters and in-laws paid graduated rates from 5% to 10%, and other individuals paid 10% to 15%. The tax was due nine months after death and was a lien on the estate for up to ten years, although a sale by a personal representative under a will's power or a court order removed the lien from the property and moved it to the proceeds (450.6, 450.7, 450.10).

For an older death, ask whether a receipt or certificate of nonliability was filed with the clerk of court.

What are the options for selling an inherited Iowa house?

An heir with legal authority can list the house on the open market, sell it at auction under court rules, or accept an as-is cash offer. Each route requires the same proof of who may sign.

A cash buyer can often close in a short time frame, which suits families who live out of state or share a house among siblings. Whichever buyer you choose, confirm the following in writing:

  • Letters of appointment, or proof that survivorship title passed.
  • Whether the will gives a power of sale, which changes the court steps.
  • Property tax status and any special assessments.
  • Who will receive proceeds, and in what order creditors are paid.

Frequently asked questions

How long does probate take in Iowa?

The statute does not set a single length. Key checkpoints include the 90-day inventory deadline after the personal representative qualifies and the creditor claim window of at least four months. Most estates with a house last longer than those checkpoints, depending on sales and disputes.

Can an Iowa heir sell a house before probate ends?

Yes, if the personal representative has authority to sell and follows the court or will provisions. A will that gives a power of sale changes the procedure, and a buyer will want letters of appointment.

Is there a small estate shortcut for a house in Iowa?

Usually no. The affidavit for very small estates requires $50,000 or less in personal property and no real property. A house is real property, so formal administration is likely.

Does Iowa charge inheritance tax now?

No for deaths on or after January 1, 2025. Estates of people who died earlier may still involve the old tax and lien rules.

What does an Iowa probate cost in court fees?

The court cost under Iowa Code 633.31 is 0.2% of the probate assets listed in the inventory for most estate services. It leaves out joint tenancy property, lifetime transfers and life insurance payable to a named beneficiary. Attorney and fiduciary fees are separate costs of administration.
